title: Cap.3 close: Word and Spirit inseparable; Cap.4 next on the states of Christ
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER FOUR follows, On ye states belonging toward Christ. — Events opposite to ye predicted outcome stand as ye casting off belonging toward Christs right, ye imputation belonging toward sin, ye denial or removal belonging toward ye Holy Spirit, and handing over into Satans power, into a reprobate mind, hardness belonging toward heart, and besides temporary evils eternal death. — Luke 7:30). — And Christ does not separate these two except by ye fault belonging toward those who despise ye Word and resist ye Holy Spirit (Acts 7:51; — And ye Word alone, apart out from ye Holy Spirits illumination and inspiration, does not suffice toward ye humans edification, as was shown above in Book I chapter 8. — For ye Holy Spirit Himself ordinarily uses ye Word or ye senses belonging toward ye Word in its external preaching (2 Corinthians 3:6). — Latin anchors: Spiritus, utitur, verbo, sensibus, verbi, ordinari, externa, praedicatione, verbum, solum, citra, Spiritus, sancti, illuminationem, inspirationem, hominis, aedificationem, sufficit, supra, demonstratum
pass_b_english: For the Holy Spirit Himself ordinarily uses the Word or the senses of the Word in its external preaching (2 Corinthians 3:6). And the Word alone, apart from the Holy Spirits illumination and inspiration, does not suffice for the humans edification, as was shown above in Book I chapter 8. And Christ does not separate these two except by the fault of those who despise the Word and resist the Holy Spirit (Acts 7:51; Luke 7:30).

Events opposite to the predicted outcome are the casting off of Christs right, the imputation of sin, the denial or removal of the Holy Spirit, and handing over into Satans power, into a reprobate mind, hardness of heart, and besides temporary evils eternal death.
CHAPTER FOUR follows, On the states of Christ.
source_text: Nam Spiritus S. ipse utitur verbo aut sensibus verbi ordinariè in eius externa praedicatione, 2 Cor. 3:6. Et verbum solum citra Spiritus sancti illuminationem & inspirationem ad hominis aedificationem non sufficit, ut supra lib. 1 cap. 8 demonstratum fuit. Et Christus haec duo non separat nisi culpa verbum contemnentium & resistantium Spiritui sancto, Act. 7:51; Luc. 7:30. Eventa apotelesmatis praedictis opposita sunt ius Christi abiectum, peccati imputatio, Spiritus S. negatio vel ablatio, & traditio in potestatem Satanae, in reprobum sensum, duritiem cordis, & praeter mala temporaria mors aeterna. CAPUT QUARTUM sequitur, De statibus Christi.
